text: In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne, and the hem of his robe filled the temple.
Above him stood seraphim, each with six wings — two covering the face, two covering the feet, and two for flying.
They called to one another: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Armies; the whole earth is full of his glory.
The doorposts and thresholds shook at the sound of their voices, and the house filled with smoke.
Then I said: Woe is me, for I am ruined! I am a man of unclean lips among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Armies.
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, holding a glowing coal he had taken from the altar with tongs.
He touched it to my mouth and said: This has touched your lips; your guilt is removed and your sin is atoned for.
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? And I said: Here I am. Send me.
He said: Go and tell this people: Keep listening, but do not understand; keep looking, but do not perceive.
Make the hearts of this people dull, their ears heavy, and their eyes blind, so that they cannot see, hear, or understand, and turn back and be healed.
Then I said: Lord, how long? And he answered: Until cities lie ruined without inhabitant, houses without people, and the land is a desolate waste.
Until the LORD has sent everyone far away and the land is utterly forsaken.
Even if a tenth remains in it, it will again be burned. But like a terebinth or oak that leaves a stump when felled, the holy seed is the stump.
